tldr: Headlines collectively portray the Trump administration as aggressively restricting immigration through simultaneous mechanisms — pausing visa processing, revoking up to 200,000 visas, and restricting student internships worldwide. Only El Pais signals in its headline that the stated justification may be a pretext; VnExpress is the sole outlet whose headlines surface both the policy crackdown and judicial pushback.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use the word 'pretext', explicitly flagging in the title itself that the 'public charge' training rationale may be a legal cover story — a skepticism no Anglophone headline in the cluster adopts.

Localizes the story as 'Nigeria: US to Revoke 200,000 Visas', using a country-specific dateline that frames the US action as a bilateral threat to Nigerian visa holders rather than a global immigration policy.

Only headline to foreground the university threat angle ('warns universities they could lose foreign students') and pair it with the punitive word 'crackdown' — amplifying institutional stakes beyond the plain policy description used by all other internship-focused outlets.

The only outlet whose headline set covers both the internship crackdown and the federal judge striking down the 75-nation visa suspension, so readers see policy action and legal constraint side by side.

bottom_line: Headline coverage presents the crackdown as accomplished fact — visa pauses, revocations, internship bans — with near-uniform policy framing across nine countries, and only El Pais and a single VnExpress headline injecting legal challenge into the title layer.
